item.title: Agentic threat actor hits the orchestration plane: AI agent-driven container escape
item.description:

Key technical details: • Exploits marimo notebook CVE-2026-39987, then enumerates Docker socket, AF_ALG kernel crypto, Copy Fail LPE paths • Creates privileged containers via Docker API to break out: `/var/run/docker.sock` mount enables host root access • Uses nsenter namespace breakout as fallback: `nsenter --target 1 --mount --uts --net --pid` • Replays stolen K8s service account token to dump entire Secret store including DB creds, API keys, SSH keys
Attack methodology: • Agent validates delivery with base64 canaries before deploying real payloads (throwaway "hello world" tests) • Structured output parsing with section markers: `echo "===SHADOW==="`, `echo "===SSH==="` • Behavioral fingerprints: acts on JSON canary tokens and invisible escape sequences humans ignore • C2: 103[.]43[.]71[.]95 🇰🇷 (origin), 43[.]167[.]11[.]88 🇸🇬 (second stage)
Hunt for privileged container creation via Docker socket with host bind mounts, base64 staging in /tmp, and K8s API calls with TLS verification disabled.

item.title: The Detection & Response Chronicles: Covert Operations Through QEMU
item.description:
NVISO investigation reveals adversaries deploying QEMU virtual machines containing malicious payloads to establish covert C2 channels, bypassing host-based AV/EDR detection through VM isolation.
Technical breakdown: • QEMU launched with Linux disk image `vault[.]db` containing SSH tunneling scripts and Adaptix C2 beacon • Port forwarding enabled via `-netdev user,id=net0,hostfwd=tcp::22022-:22` for SSH access on port 22022 • Persistence via crontab executing `/sbin/syslogdb.sh` (SSH tunnel) and `/sbin/syslogda.sh` (C2 beacon) at boot • SSH tunnel to C2 over TCP 443 with local port forwarding: `-L 127.0.0.1:33443:127.0.0.1:33443` • Alternative technique uses QEMU socket networking for tunneling without disk image transfer
MITRE TTPs: • T1055.012 (Process Hollowing via VM isolation) • T1572 (Protocol Tunneling via SSH over 443) • T1053.003 (Cron-based persistence)
Detection opportunities: • Monitor QEMU execution from unusual locations (`\Users\`, `\temp\`, `/tmp/`, `/home/`) • Hunt for suspicious networking args: `hostfwd=`, `restrict=off`, `listen=`, `connect=` • Alert on renamed QEMU binaries with characteristic command-line arguments • Flag low memory allocation (`-m <100M`) combined with `-nographic` options
Full KQL hunting queries provided in the report for detecting QEMU abuse across Windows environments.

item.title: The KQL Query That Caught 260 Brute Force Attempts in Microsoft Sentinel
item.description:

Technical breakdown: • Rule queries Syslog table filtering authpriv facility for "Failed password" and "authentication failure" messages • Uses bin(TimeGenerated, 5m) to aggregate events into 5-minute windows, counting failures per timeframe • Threshold set at >10 failures per 5-minute window to distinguish automated attacks from legitimate user errors • Maps to MITRE T1110.001 (Brute Force: Password Guessing) with High severity auto-incident generation • Attack sourced from 10.0.0.100 targeting Ubuntu server with zero successful authentications
